claims.text: The material is HfNbTiVAl10 with a hierarchical heterostructure.
A machine-learning model can predict the Young's modulus of hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10 more accurately than established simulations.
A machine-learning model can predict the yield strength of hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10 more accurately than established simulations.
A machine-learning model can predict the fracture-related behavior of hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10 more accurately than established simulations.
The machine-learning model can make these predictions more rapidly than established simulations.
The machine-learning model is trained on a dataset of hierarchical heterostructures.
Training on hierarchical heterostructures enables improved predictive accuracy and efficiency for hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10.
The proposed comparison applies under tensile and fracture testing.
The scope of the hypothesis is limited to HfNbTiVAl10 with a hierarchical heterostructure.
The exact magnitude of improvement cannot be determined from the available data.
Predictive performance can be compared using mean absolute error and computational time.
